mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPI YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased wage pressures and higher corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO MoM < -1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS MoM > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals a strong labor market, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS MoM > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as market participants anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 QoQ < -0.5%.
